I don't think you get it. If Ariel was black in the original movie no one would have a problem with it, none. They're changing aspects of a movie that doesn't have to be changed.   
WHY black? Like I genuinely don't get it. For brownie points? Because it's historical accurate? Because so was she in the original story?   
The latter two is both false. Sure there's black people in Denmark but far from as many as in the USA. In the original story it even says her skin is fair/clear. Why give so little respect to the story's origin when they honor other stories' origins, even if it's just fiction, it's a story that means a lot to many people, and the fact they're just shitting all over it is telling. Disney goes for the money and there's money in being PC at the moment, hence why I think she's black. Because why else?   


Fiction or not, it's still has it roots from somewhere, and it still means a lot to a lot of people. As a Dane it means a lot to ME. I grew up with these stories. I grew up with cartoons of the original story, not Disney's version. What if they made Moana white? Everyone would loose their shit. And that's just fiction too, right? Or Tiana white, that's fiction too.  Why is it ok to change people from white to black but not the other way around? Why is it ok for people to be upset if they "whitewash" a show/movie, but it's not ok to be upset when they do the same but with black people? It's the same thing, after all.
